fix: Include `maintenanceWorker` and `exportWorker` in the /readyz check (or document why they're excluded), and have the boot `.catch` handlers retry-with-backoff or flip a fatal flag so the process is restarted rather than silently degraded. Update the stale 'both BullMQ workers' comment.

title: Overdue reminder idempotency key is pinned to the loan's fixed dueAt → a member is nagged exactly once, ever
description: The overdue key is `overdue:${ctx.id}:${loan.id}:${dayKey(loan.dueAt)}` (member-notifications.job.ts:253). `dayKey(d) = new Date(d).toISOString().slice(0,10)` (line 30) and `loan.dueAt` is fixed for the loan's life, so the key never changes across hourly sweeps. EmailService dedups on the unique idempotencyKey constraint, returning `alreadyExisted` (email.service.ts:114-125), and the job only counts `if (!res.alreadyExisted)` (line 256). So a loan overdue for weeks gets exactly ONE overdue reminder, dated to its due day. The registry comment claims overdue is 'day-grained so re-runs within a day are idempotent' (registry.ts:64-66) — it is actually loan-lifetime-grained. (due-soon shares the property but single-send is intended there.)
impact: Members are never re-reminded about long-overdue items, undercutting the recovery purpose of the reminder. No data/security impact — product/correctness only.
fix: If repeated nags are intended, key on the current day, e.g. `overdue:${ctx.id}:${loan.id}:${dayKey(now)}`, and/or add a configurable cadence; otherwise correct the misleading registry comment to state overdue sends once.

title: scheduled-jobs /healthz lastResults only records successes — ongoing job failures are invisible
description: `lastResults[job.name]` is set only after `def.handler(ctx)` resolves (scheduled-jobs.runner.ts:83-87); the `finally` only does `inFlight--` (line 91-93). On a throw the error propagates to BullMQ and is logged by `worker.on('failed')` to stderr (line 98-100), but `lastResults` keeps the last SUCCESS snapshot. /healthz surfaces `scheduledLastResults: scheduledJobs?.lastResults()` (worker.ts:67), so an operator sees a stale 'ok' for a job failing every tick. No `attempts`/`backoff` is configured on the repeatable jobs (runner.ts:57-66 — only `repeat`, `removeOnComplete`, `removeOnFail`).
impact: Silent, ongoing scheduled-job failures (e.g. a consistently-unreachable tenant DB, or fine-accrual throwing) are not reflected in the health surface ops watch; only stderr shows them. Observability gap only.
fix: Record failures into lastResults too (e.g. `{ at, message: 'FAILED: …', ok: false }`) and/or expose a per-job failure counter/last-error in /metrics so failures are observable without log scraping.

title: Stripe retry sweep's BillingService/EffectivePlanService share one RedisService whose only teardown is in finally — an early throw before the loop leaks the connection
description: The sweep constructs `const redis = new RedisService()` at line 54, then builds settings/effective/driver/billing (lines 55-60) BEFORE entering the `try { … } finally { await redis.onModuleDestroy() }` block (lines 65-87). The `redis.onModuleDestroy()` teardown only runs if execution reaches the try. The constructors between line 54 and 65 are unlikely to throw, so the window is small, but any throw in `new PlatformSettingsService`/`new EffectivePlanService`/driver construction (e.g. RealStripeDriver reading a missing key at construction time) would leak the Redis socket opened at line 54. Contrast with member-notifications.job.ts which has the same shape (line 135-156) — both rely on construction never throwing after the Redis open.
impact: A leaked ioredis connection per failed sweep tick if a collaborator constructor throws. Bounded and low-probability, but accumulates across ticks until the process restarts.
fix: Open Redis inside the try, or wrap construction so the `finally` teardown always covers the connection (move `const redis = new RedisService()` to just before `try`, and ensure all subsequent construction is inside the try).

title: billingEnabled doc comment says default `true`, code defaults to `false` (fail-open vs fail-closed contradiction)
description: env.ts:89 doc comment ends 'Default `true`.' The parser at env.ts:229-231 is `billingEnabled: ['true','1','yes','on'].includes((process.env.BILLING_ENABLED ?? '').toLowerCase().trim())` — unset/empty/non-truthy ⇒ false. The inline rationale at :223-228 explicitly documents this is intentional (the old `true` default + `??` not catching empty string silently enforced Starter). So the surviving comment at :89 directly contradicts the code. Operationally, when BILLING_ENABLED is unset AND the admin Subscriptions toggle is off, getEffectivePlan returns unlimitedPlan() (effective-plan.service.ts:96-97, 43-55), unenforcing all quotas/flags — but that is also subject to the platform_settings runtime toggle, so the stale comment is the only defect; behavior itself is the safe choice.
impact: Misleading documentation on a master enforcement switch; an operator trusting the stale 'Default true' could misjudge whether plan limits are active in a fresh deploy. No runtime security/data impact.
fix: Update the EnvConfig.billingEnabled doc comment at env.ts:89 to state the default is OFF when unset, matching the parser and the :223-228 rationale.

title: Passively-expired tenant_plan_overrides keep elevated limits for up to the plan cache TTL (no expiry-driven invalidation)
description: Resolver SQL filters expired overrides at the DB level only: effective-plan.service.ts:171 `AND (tpo."expiresAt" IS NULL OR tpo."expiresAt" > NOW())`. But writeCache stores a single flat-TTL blob: :240-242 `redis.client.set(CACHE_KEY(tenantId), JSON.stringify(plan), 'EX', this.ttlSec)` with ttlSec = tenantCacheTtlSec (env.ts:162 default 300). getEffectivePlan (:86-98) serves the cached blob until TTL or explicit invalidate(). Grep of `.invalidate(` shows it is called ONLY on override create/edit (admin-overrides.controller.ts:115,126), plan edits (admin-plans.controller.ts:191), and subscription/billing changes (billing.service.ts:*, admin-tenants.controller.ts:181) — there is NO scheduler or delayed job keyed on expiresAt. The class doc-comment at :64-67 even claims invalidation happens when an override is 'expired', but no such mechanism exists. So for up to ttlSec after expiresAt, the QuotaInterceptor / PlanGuard / enforceWithinTx (all via getInt→cached plan) keep honoring the lapsed override.
impact: Bounded (≤ cache TTL, default 5 min) over-grant of a feature/quota after a time-based override expires. Auto-recovers on TTL or any invalidating mutation. Limited blast radius, requires an admin to have set a time-boxed override in the first place.
fix: On override save, schedule an invalidation at expiresAt (small BullMQ delayed job), or have writeCache cap the blob's TTL at the soonest upcoming override expiry for that tenant; and fix the :64-67 comment which falsely claims expiry-driven invalidation already happens.

title: EffectivePlanService doc comment falsely claims expired overrides trigger cache invalidation
description: The class doc-comment lists the invalidation triggers as: subscription changes, plan_feature_value changes, and 'a tenant_plan_override for the tenant changes (created / edited / expired)'. The word 'expired' implies time-based expiry invalidates the cache, but there is no scheduler, delayed job, or hook anywhere that fires on expiresAt — grep of `.invalidate(` shows only mutation-driven callers (admin-overrides 115/126, admin-plans 191, billing.service.*, admin-tenants 181). Expiry is handled solely by the DB-level SQL filter at :171 on the NEXT cache miss. A maintainer reading this comment would wrongly conclude the over-grant window of PQF-3 cannot happen.
impact: Misleading invariant documentation directly adjacent to a real staleness bug (PQF-3); increases the chance the over-grant window is dismissed as already-handled during future review.
fix: Remove '/ expired' from the comment at effective-plan.service.ts:67, or implement the expiry-driven invalidation the comment promises.

title: Announcement email enqueued before the delivery row is created, inside a GET read path
description: ensureDelivery() runs inside activeForUser() (called from the GET /t/:slug/announcements/active route, tenant-announcements.controller.ts:31-46). The email enqueue (lines 252-260) executes BEFORE the announcementDelivery.create (lines 269-277). If create throws and the post-conflict re-read (lines 280-287) also finds no winner, it `throw err` (line 288) → 5xx to the user, but the email was already enqueued. The enqueue itself is wrapped in its own try/catch that only logs a warning (lines 262-266), so an enqueue failure does NOT break the read. idempotencyKey is tenant-scoped so concurrent first-fetches dedupe — the smell is a side-effecting send ordered before its own bookkeeping row inside a cacheable GET.
impact: Edge case: an email can be sent while the controlling delivery row failed to persist, so in-app stats undercount and a transient DB error on a GET returns 5xx yet still fired mail. Low blast radius — the unique idempotencyKey prevents duplicates across retries.
fix: Create the delivery row first (or in the same transaction) and enqueue the email only after it commits; move announcement materialization out of the cache-miss read path into the publish cron.

title: Web /api/readyz fetch to the API has no timeout — probe can hang
description: route.ts:17 `const res = await fetch(`${apiBase.replace(/\/$/, '')}/readyz`, { cache: 'no-store' })` — no AbortController/signal/timeout. undici defaults (headersTimeout/bodyTimeout ~300s) mean a half-open API socket can hang this handler far beyond the orchestrator window. NOTE: the compose web healthcheck probes `/api/healthz` (docker-compose.prod.yml:203), not `/api/readyz`, and has its own `timeout: 5s`; the wget probe is what's actually cut at 5s, so the hung handler invocation just leaks until undici times out rather than blocking the healthcheck verdict. Real but minor.
impact: A wedged API can make this readiness handler hang (resource held open until undici's long default timeout) rather than failing fast as not_ready. Low severity because the orchestrator healthcheck has its own 5s timeout and targets /api/healthz.
fix: Add an AbortController with a ~3s timeout to the fetch and treat the abort as not_ready (503).

title: No process-level unhandledRejection / uncaughtException handlers in API or worker
description: grep across apps/api/src for unhandledRejection/uncaughtException returns only worker.ts:209-210 (SIGTERM/SIGINT). main.ts:55-58 only `.catch`es the bootstrap() promise. The worker fans out five fire-and-forget start promises (worker.ts:123-173) whose .catch only console.error. No top-level unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handler exists in either entrypoint. Note: NestJS's HttpExceptionFilter (registered main.ts:36) catches per-request errors via Express — this finding is only about truly uncaught/unhandled rejections outside the request lifecycle (e.g. background async paths).
impact: A stray uncaught exception or unhandled rejection (e.g. in a background async path) under Node's default --unhandled-rejections=throw terminates the process without a structured/greppable log line and bypasses the graceful shutdown() drain, leaving in-flight BullMQ jobs/connections uncleaned. Low severity — most real error surfaces are already covered by the Nest exception filter and per-handle .catch logging.
fix: Register top-level unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers in both main.ts and worker.ts that log via the structured logger and trigger graceful shutdown (or exit non-zero after flushing).

title: New fine de-dup migration uses CREATE UNIQUE INDEX without IF NOT EXISTS — not re-runnable after a partial-apply failure
description: migration.sql:33-35 ends with `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "fines_one_outstanding_per_loan" ON "fines" ("loanId") WHERE "status" = 'outstanding' AND "loanId" IS NOT NULL;` — no IF NOT EXISTS. The dedup WITH-ranked/UPDATE (lines 15-31) is idempotent and the partial predicate correctly excludes loanId-NULL and resolved fines, so the logic is sound. The cited precedent is real but lives in db-control, not db-tenant: 20260528200000_announcements_partial_unique/migration.sql:7 uses `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "announcement_deliveries_tenant_wide_unique"`. Migrations are applied via the standard once-only path (tenant-migrate.ts:126 `prisma migrate deploy`), so under normal operation this never re-runs — only a partial-apply (connection drop after DDL, before history row) wedges the tenant with `relation already exists` / P3009.
impact: A partially-applied migration on one tenant DB wedges that tenant's migration history (P3009) and needs manual `prisma migrate resolve`, blocking later migrations for that DB. Low: Prisma's once-only guarantee makes this an operational edge case, not a normal-path bug.
fix: Use `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "fines_one_outstanding_per_loan" …`, matching the precedent already set in the control-plane announcements_partial_unique migration.

title: Return transaction can roll back under concurrency because the duplicate-fine create is inside the return TX
description: In returnLoan the fine create runs inside the same `$transaction` that closed the loan at loans.service.ts:445-453 and freed the copy at 462-465: loans.service.ts:479-500 does `tx.fine.findFirst({ where: { loanId, status: 'outstanding' } })` then `tx.fine.create(...)`. markLost is identical (loans.service.ts:683-704). translate() at 880-883 maps `code === 'P2002'` to a ConflictException. So if the accrual sweep inserts the outstanding fine in the window between findFirst (sees none) and create, the in-TX create raises P2002, aborting the ENTIRE return/mark-lost transaction (loan close + copy free roll back). By contrast the accrual job's create is standalone and explicitly swallows P2002 (fine-accrual.job.ts:131-136 `if (!isUniqueViolation(err)) throw err`), confirming the asymmetry. No double charge or corruption — just a spurious 409 forcing a retry.
impact: Occasional spurious 409 ("refresh and try again") on return / mark-lost for an overdue item when the accrual cron fires in the same sub-second window; the librarian must retry once. No data corruption, no money error.
fix: Catch P2002 on the in-TX fine.create and fall back to updating the now-existing outstanding fine. Note: because Postgres aborts a transaction after a statement error, the catch must wrap the create in a SAVEPOINT (Prisma interactive-tx nested call) or do the find-then-update under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` / advisory lock so the whole return completes on first attempt instead of rolling back.

title: prod compose `app` network is internal:false, so any future host-port publish or extra service is internet-exposed by default
description: docker-compose.prod.yml:305-307 declares `app: driver: bridge / internal: false # set to \`true\` post-MVP if egress through caddy only`. Verified the backstop holds TODAY: the only `ports:` block in the whole file is Caddy at lines 93-96 (`'80:80' '443:443' '443:443/udp'`), and Caddy is the only service on `edge` (line 113 `networks: [edge, app]`); postgres/redis/pgbouncer/api/web/worker/migrate are all `networks: [app]` with no host-port mapping. So no active data-tier exposure exists. The risk is exactly as described: with internal:false the only thing preventing exposure is the discipline of never adding a `ports:` block to an app-network service.
impact: No active exposure today. Latent: a future service added with a `ports:` mapping, or a `docker run --network <proj>_app -p`, would directly expose Postgres/Redis (whose only auth is POSTGRES_PASSWORD/scram).
fix: Split networks so the data tier sits on an `internal: true` network that only api/web/worker/caddy join, or at minimum document that NO service on `app` may ever declare `ports:`. The single Caddy-on-both-networks topology already supports tightening this now.

title: Collections un-archive quota check false-rejects a no-op edit when the tenant is exactly at max_custom_collections
description: collections.service.ts:152 sets `const isRestore = input.archived === false;` with NO check that the row is actually archived. When isRestore, it runs enforceWithinTx counting `tx.collection.count({ where: { archivedAt: null } })` (line 190) BEFORE tx.collection.update writes archivedAt — so for an already-active collection the count includes the row itself. books.service.ts:352 avoids this exactly: `const restoring = input.archived === false && existing.archivedAt != null;`. The collections code also lacks that conjunct.
impact: A tenant at exactly max_custom_collections that issues a no-op edit setting `archived: false` on an already-active collection (e.g. a UI save that always sends the flag) trips a spurious 402 Payment Required, blocking legitimate customization. Narrow blast radius (only at the exact limit, only collections), but a real bug introduced/left by the remediation that books does not have.
fix: Mirror books: resolve the row first and only treat it as a quota-consuming restore when it was actually archived — `isRestore = input.archived === false && existing.archivedAt != null`. Resolve existing.archivedAt before deciding whether to enforce.

title: Stripe-retry sweep re-dispatches without the Redis lock — narrow double-processing window
description: The controller now persists the row BEFORE the lock (stripe-webhook.controller.ts:73-99), so an in-flight event has a row with processedAt=null, error=null. The sweep selects `processedAt: null AND (error != null OR receivedAt < now-5min)` (stripe-retry.job.ts:40-44) and dispatches at line 69 WITHOUT ever referencing EVENT_KEY / acquiring the controller's Redis lock (grep confirms no lock acquisition in stripe-retry.job.ts). So if a single controller dispatch outlives the 5-min staleBefore window, the sweep can run the same event concurrently. HOWEVER the mechanics-only concern overstates impact: the handlers are absolute idempotent writes — recordPaymentSuccess sets `{status:'active', graceUntil:null}` (billing.service.ts:419-422), recordPaymentFailure sets `{status:'past_due', graceUntil: now+Ndays}` (billing.service.ts:409-412), syncStripeSubscription is an upsert. None are additive, so re-applying the same event does not double-count money. The Stripe client timeout is 10s with maxNetworkRetries=2 (stripe-real.driver.ts:42-43), and these handlers do control-DB writes (not chained Stripe API calls), making a >5-min single dispatch implausible.
impact: A rare concurrent re-dispatch of one in-flight webhook during a pathological slowdown. No money loss / corruption because all side effects are idempotent absolute writes; the only observable drift is recordPaymentFailure recomputing graceUntil = now+N days on the second run, slightly EXTENDING the grace window (customer-favorable, harmless). The reviewer's 'double-count payment success/failure' does not actually occur.
fix: Low priority. For belt-and-suspenders, have the sweep SET NX the same EVENT_KEY before dispatching and skip rows whose lock is still held; the handlers are already effectively idempotent so this is hardening, not a fix for an active money bug.

title: Atomic write uses a predictable temp name and doesn't lock down the parent directory
description: saveModel (540-549) writes to a predictable `${model.path}.tmp-${process.pid}` (544) via `writeFileSync(tmp, body, { mode: 0o600 })` (545, default 'w' flag follows symlinks and does not fail if target exists), then chmod (546) then rename (547). `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` (542) creates parent dirs with default perms (0777 & ~umask), not 0700. The file mode is correctly forced to 0600, but the temp name is guessable and the dir is not locked to 0700.
impact: Low in the intended root-owned /srv/libriant deployment, but the tool also targets ./.env.prod / arbitrary --file paths in possibly shared or world-traversable dirs, where the predictable temp name + symlink-following write is a minor local hardening gap.
fix: Use an O_EXCL/randomized temp name in the same dir, write with the 'wx' flag, and create parent dirs with mode 0o700. Optionally fstat the target to detect a symlink before renaming over it.

title: actionSet explicit-value path can throw an uncaught error from serializeKV (single-quote value) instead of a friendly message
description: When `set KEY VALUE` is called with an explicit value, actionSet runs only `def.validate` (898-903) then calls `setValue(model, key, next)` (905) which invokes serializeKV. For a value containing a single quote, serializeKV throws (526-528). Unlike promptValue (869-874) which wraps serializeKV in a try/catch and re-prompts, the explicit-value path has no guard, so the throw propagates to main().catch (1232-1235) and the process exits 1 with a raw error line. Most managed keys have no `validate`, so e.g. `pnpm secrets set RCLONE_REMOTE "o'brien:bucket"` crashes the tool rather than reporting a clean validation message.
impact: Minor: an operator setting a value containing a single quote gets an abrupt exit-1 mid-task rather than a graceful '✗ ...' message and re-prompt. No data loss (write is aborted before saveModel), but inconsistent UX and could be mistaken for a tool bug.
fix: Wrap the serializeKV/setValue call in actionSet's explicit-value path in a try/catch that prints the friendly message (as promptValue does), or validate the value can be stored before attempting the write.

title: Sticky mobile top bar (z-index:50) stacks above combobox dropdowns (z-index:20)
description: `.lbr-shell__topbar` is `position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 50;` (styles.css:612-614) and the autocomplete dropdown `.lbr-combobox__listbox` is `position: absolute; ...; z-index: 20;` (styles.css:783-797). The listbox's nearest positioned ancestor `.lbr-combobox` is `position: relative` with NO z-index (styles.css:780-782), so it does not create a stacking context — the listbox's z-index:20 competes directly with the topbar's z-index:50 in the same (root) stacking context, and 50 > 20. The dropdown opens downward (`top: calc(100% + var(--sp-1))`, styles.css:785), so overlap with the sticky topbar band occurs only when the combobox field is scrolled to sit right under the bar while focused/open — a real but narrow condition.
impact: In narrow viewports, a combobox option list can be partially painted over by the sticky header when the field scrolls up under the bar, making upper options hard to click. Cosmetic/usability, narrow trigger.
fix: Give `.lbr-combobox__listbox` a z-index above the topbar (>50), or render the listbox in a portal/top layer so the sticky header can't overlap it.

title: Card-reflow wrapper relies on :has() for its cosmetic fallback; unsupported browsers show a double border
description: `.lbr-table-wrap` base sets `overflow-x: auto; border-radius: var(--radius-lg); border: 1px solid var(--color-border-muted);` (styles.css:1063-1066). The card reflow under `@media (max-width:768px)` (styles.css:1073+) turns rows into stacked cards WITHOUT using :has(). The only thing that strips the wrapper's now-redundant scroll box + border is `.lbr-table-wrap:has(.lbr-table--cards) { overflow-x: visible; border: 0; }` (styles.css:1119), which depends on :has(). On any engine lacking :has() support, that rule is dropped and the wrapper keeps its rounded border + horizontal-scroll box around the already-stacked cards. Cards still render; only the outer border is redundant. Modern Next.js baseline supports :has(), so blast radius is small.
impact: Purely cosmetic double border around DataTable card stacks on older engines lacking :has(); no functional or layout break.
fix: Make the fallback non-:has()-dependent — e.g. add a plain `.lbr-table-wrap--cards` modifier on the wrapper alongside `.lbr-table--cards` and target it directly for the border/overflow reset.

title: sanitiseFilename does not strip double-quote or CR/LF from the Content-Disposition filename
description: sendFile sets `'content-disposition': `attachment; filename="${sanitiseFilename(filename)}"`` (line 216), and sanitiseFilename only strips backslash/slash/NUL: `name.replace(/[\\/\0]/g, '_').slice(0, 200)` (line 226) — leaves literal `"`, CR, LF intact. Confirmed not exploitable today: the authenticated download requires the ref to pass safeResolve + stat (file must exist), and stored filenames are server-generated `cuidLike()+ext` (local-driver.ts:144-146, pickExtension restricts ext to `/^\.[a-z0-9]{1,6}$/`), so a passing ref can't carry a quote/CRLF; the signed endpoint uses `payload.fn` set server-side from the URL :filename at signing time. Node's HTTP layer also rejects CR/LF in header values. Latent only — would become a Content-Disposition injection vector if a future driver/rename path ever lets client-controlled filenames reach this sink.
impact: No exploitable path today; the sanitizer is incomplete and is a latent header-injection gap if filenames ever become attacker-influenced. Downgraded from low to info given no current reachability.
fix: Also strip/replace `"`, CR, LF and control chars, and prefer RFC 5987 `filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded>` with an ASCII `filename=` fallback.

title: Storage security primitives have zero automated test coverage
description: `find apps/api -path '*storage*' -name '*.spec.ts'` returns nothing, and `grep -rln 'safeResolve|SignedUrlService|_files/signed|LocalDriver'` over *.spec.ts returns nothing — no tests for safeResolve (the path-traversal defense at local-driver.ts:99-108), SignedUrlService sign/verify (tenant binding/expiry/tamper), the public _files/signed endpoint, the quota check, or the MIME allowlist. The safeResolve logic as written is correct (rejects '', '..', NUL at line 100,104 and post-resolve escape at line 106), but no test guards against regression.
impact: A future refactor could silently reintroduce path traversal, weaken signed-token tenant binding, or break the MIME gate with no failing test. High-blast-radius code with no safety net.
fix: Add unit tests for safeResolve (`../`, leading `/`, `\0`, valid refs), SignedUrlService (cross-tenant/expired/tampered tokens), and an integration test asserting the signed endpoint rejects a token whose tid != requested tenant and that downloads are octet-stream + attachment.

title: Downloads read entire file into memory (no streaming) — bounded by upload cap but worth noting
description: Both the authenticated download (lines 98-100) and the public signed download (lines 165-168) buffer the whole file: `const buf = await this.storage.get(tenant, ref)` → LocalDriver.get → `fs.readFile(p)` (local-driver.ts:70-73), then `res.send(buf)` (line 220). No streaming, no read-side size cap. Per-request memory is bounded by the upload ceiling (default 25MB) but amplifies with STG-02 (a disabled cap) and many concurrent large downloads. S3Driver.get is an unimplemented stub (s3-driver.ts:38-40), so today this applies only to LocalDriver.
impact: Higher per-request memory footprint than necessary; amplifies the DoS surface if the upload cap is misconfigured. Acceptable for MVP scale but should stream for large files / future S3.
fix: Stream the body (createReadStream → res for local; GetObject body stream for S3) and add a read-side guard; the driver interface already anticipates a streaming overload.

title: Prototype pollution and transform ReDoS surfaces examined and found SAFE (verification note)
description: Confirmed the analysis: tabular.ts:73-77 assigns `cells[columns[c]!.name] = cellsArr[c] ?? ''` onto a plain object — a header literally named __proto__ assigns to the proto slot as a silent no-op (no own prop, Object.prototype untouched) and is dropped by Object.keys downstream; marc-parser.ts:36-42 setKey `rec[key] = ...` is the same pattern. Custom-field keys are independently constrained by FIELD_KEY_RE `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,49}$/` (import.service.ts:21) which rejects __proto__/constructor. splitMulti escapes its separators into a quantifier-free character class (transforms.ts:190) so it is ReDoS-immune, and multiSeparators is admin-controlled via cleanOptions (import.service.ts:304), not file-controlled. The regexes in transforms.ts (toYear, toDateIso, normalizeIsbn13, etc.) are linear with no nested quantifiers.
impact: None — documents that prototype-pollution and ReDoS import vectors were checked and are not exploitable here.
fix: No action required. Optionally use Object.create(null) / Map for parser cell records as defense-in-depth.

title: Web /api/metrics route is publicly reachable and leaks NODE_ENV
description: GET /api/metrics (route.ts:13) has no auth and emits libriant_web_uptime_seconds (route.ts:18) and libriant_web_build_info{node_env="${process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development'}"} (route.ts:21). It is served by Caddy's catch-all `handle { reverse_proxy web:3000 }` (Caddyfile:161). The Caddy @is_probe matcher (Caddyfile:59) only matches the literal paths /healthz /readyz /metrics — NOT /api/metrics — so the request reaches the Next.js handler. Confirmed reachable and unauthenticated.
impact: Low. Only process uptime (hints at recent restarts/deploys) and the NODE_ENV string are exposed; no tenant or business data. Minor reconnaissance surface.
fix: Gate /api/metrics behind the internal network / allowlist together with the WEB-01 metrics fix, or drop the node_env label from route.ts:21.

title: dueSoonDays column has no non-negative CHECK constraint (others on tenant_settings do)
description: member_notification_settings/migration.sql:5 adds `dueSoonDays INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 2` with no CHECK, and it is not folded into the init `tenant_settings_nonneg` CHECK (20260526184041_init/migration.sql:551-560 covers loanPeriodDays/maxRenewals/finePerDayCents/fineCapCents/holdPickupHours/maxActiveLoans only) — so the missing-constraint observation is factually correct. HOWEVER the finding's cited impact ("a negative value would compute a window in the past and the reminder would never fire") is FALSE: the API DTO validates `@Min(1) @Max(60)` on dueSoonDays (tenant-settings.dto.ts:100-101), and the due-soon job clamps defensively with `Math.max(1, settings.dueSoonDays)` (member-notifications.job.ts:188), so even a negative DB value yields a 1-day window, not a past one — reminders still fire.
impact: Pure schema-consistency / defense-in-depth gap with no functional consequence given the DTO @Min(1) bound and the Math.max(1, …) clamp in the job. Downgraded from low to info because the asserted concrete harm cannot occur.
fix: Optional consistency: add `ALTER TABLE tenant_settings ADD CONSTRAINT tenant_settings_due_soon_days_nonneg CHECK ("dueSoonDays" >= 1)` to match the existing tenant_settings_nonneg pattern. No code change needed since the job already clamps.

title: migrate one-shot bootstrap container runs as root
description: docker-compose.prod.yml:135 sets `user: root` on the `migrate` service, with the comment at 132-134 explaining it reuses a root-prepared corepack cache and only does DB DDL. Confirmed it is a scoped ephemeral one-shot: `restart: 'no'` (line 131), `command: ['sh', '/app/scripts/prod-bootstrap.sh']` (136), `depends_on: postgres: service_healthy` (141-143), repo scripts/locales mounted read-only (144-146), `networks: [app]` only (147), no `ports:`. The long-running api/web/worker services run as the image's `node` user. Accurate as written.
impact: Negligible — ephemeral, no listening ports, exits before api/worker serve traffic. The only enlarged blast radius is that this short-lived root container holds PG_SUPERUSER_URL.
fix: Optional: pre-warm the corepack cache for uid 1000 in the Dockerfile so the migrate one-shot can also run as `node`, eliminating the only root container in the prod stack.

title: IMPERSONATION_SECRET classified rotation 'safe' / 'users unaffected' but rotating it kills in-progress support sessions
description: IMPERSONATION_SECRET is `rotation: 'safe'` (secrets.ts:128) with note 'Ends any in-progress support/impersonation sessions; users unaffected.' (129). The comparable SESSION_SECRET/ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET are 'caution' (97,113). Ending active support sessions mid-incident is a real (low-blast-radius) side effect the 'safe' label understates.
impact: Advisory only: an operator trusting 'safe' might rotate it during an active support session and drop it. No security/data impact.
fix: Either keep 'safe' with softer wording, or bump to 'caution' for consistency with the other session-signing secrets. Cosmetic.

title: Dead CSS utility .lbr-cluster is defined and shipped but never used; commit message claims it is applied
description: `.lbr-cluster { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--sp-2); align-items: center; }` is defined at styles.css:1041 and is the ONLY occurrence of the token in source — a grep over apps/web/app, apps/web/components and packages/ui/src for `lbr-cluster` returns just that definition (0 TSX usages), whereas `lbr-form-grid` is used across 4 files and `lbr-split` across 8. The class is dead CSS and the commit message overstates that layouts collapse via `.lbr-cluster`.
impact: Negligible: a few unused CSS rules and a slightly inaccurate commit message. No runtime effect.
fix: Either apply `.lbr-cluster` where horizontal button/filter groups currently use inline flex-wrap, or drop the unused rule.
